title: When to change the target mix
objectives: List the valid reasons to change the target mix.
Explain why a market view or last year's returns are not reasons.
body_md:
Rebalancing returns to the target. Changing the target is a different, bigger decision, and only three things justify it.

## The valid reasons

- A goal comes within 3–5 years: start the glide path.
- Life changes: marriage, a child, a new loan, job loss, an inheritance, retirement.
- The risk profile changes: re-run the questionnaire every 2–3 years or after a life event.

## What is never a reason

A market view, a news headline, last year's returns, or a friend's portfolio. These change the noise, not the client's goal, horizon or capacity.

## How to handle it

When a client asks to change the mix after a strong year for one asset, the answer is: the target was set from your goal and your profile, and neither has changed. If the profile has changed, we will re-run it and document the new target.

The target mix and the rebalancing rules belong in writing, agreed with the client.
example: After gold's strong year, a client wants 40% gold. The target stays at 10%: the goal is unchanged and the profile is unchanged. The band rule may trim or top up, but the target is not rewritten because of one year.
say: We change the target when your goal or your profile changes, not when an asset has a good year.
Let's re-run the risk profile and put the new target in writing.
never: Gold did well, so let's make it the core holding.
Let's change the mix because the market looks shaky.

talk_track.title: Change the target only for goals, life events or a new risk profile
talk_track.text: Change the target itself only for goals, life events or a new risk profile, never because of a market view. Rebalancing brings the mix back to the target; changing the target is a bigger decision that belongs in writing.

check.q: Which is a good reason to change the target mix?
o: A goal is now within 3 years
check.why: Goals, life events and a changed risk profile justify a new target.

check.q: What is the difference between rebalancing and changing the target?
o: Rebalancing returns to the agreed target; changing the target sets a new one
Changing the target needs no documentation
check.why: Rebalancing is maintenance. Changing the target is a new decision, and it belongs in writing.

check.q: When should the target mix be reviewed?
o: When a goal comes within 3–5 years, after a life event, or when the risk profile changes
check.why: Those three triggers, plus a routine re-run of the risk profile every two to three years.
